findings.reason: The only check the Host actually ran on e0d9020 is diff-check, which passed. The developer says the migration, deletion, Git and connection tests, the typecheck and the UI build all passed, but no Host check backs that. I also couldn't confirm from this read-only checkout that both PR head 92bc71c and main 6d690fb are ancestors of this commit. I checked the code itself: main's 0017_api_connection_deletion.sql and 0018_connection_verifications.sql are untouched. The Worktree migration is now 0019, and its SQL differs from before only in the version number. Fresh databases get 17, 18 and 19 in order. An old Worktree-branch database is recognized by three things together: version 17 recorded, the worktree_removals table present, and no api_connections.deleted_at column. Its version-17 record is renamed to 19 with the original applied_at kept. Main's 17 and 18 then run, all in one transaction that rolls back if anything fails. Databases already on main's 17 or 18 only get the migrations they are missing. tests/core/connection-worktree-migration.test.ts covers fresh, main 16/17/18 and old Worktree 17 upgrades, rollback with a safe retry, reopening, data retention, foreign keys, credential ownership and the deletion safety triggers. host-service.ts keeps main's connection delete and verify routes, the Host default-Lead guard and the diagnostics routes, and also the PR's strict worktree-removals delete/reconcile routes and the archive guards.
findings.suggestion: Before the plain push that updates PR #2, run `git merge-base --is-ancestor` for 92bc71c and 6d690fb against e0d9020. Also run the targeted vitest suites, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build:ui` on this exact commit, unless Host check evidence for them is attached.
